exact_missing_items: Canonical state/action labels must include: Locally Complete, Seam Complete, Completion Blocked, Weak Integration, Promotion Blocked, Promotion Revoked, Corroboration Requested, Challenge Accepted, Challenge Not Accepted, Advisory Concern Recorded, Graph Patch Requested, Graph Patch Applied, Generation Updated
Promotion labels must be: 'Lane to Package' (lane_to_package), 'Package to Seam' (package_to_seam_available), 'Seam Completion' (seam_complete)
Revocation and reopen labels must be: Promotion Revoked, Seam Completion Revoked, Reopened, Reopened by Patch, Reopened by New Evidence
Blocked ownership labels must be a closed vocabulary: Runtime, Package Overseer, Seam Overseer, Corroboration, Graph Patch, Recovery, User, External Resource
Feature seam is a first-class governance scope: seam completion requires integration quality across packages, not just local package-pass states

Weak-integration categories (10): GUI/runtime mismatch, incomplete end-to-end flow, cross-package state mismatch, contract drift, technically-wired-but-operationally-unusable, local-pass/global-fail, missing degraded/recovery behavior, inconsistent UX semantics, cross-seam architecture drift, invisible governance/missing operator affordances
Seam-level acceptance dimensions (5): operability, state coherence, workflow completeness, UX coherence, architectural coherence
Completion state progression must follow: Locally Complete → Available to Seam → Seam Complete; each transition has defined gates
Canonical event families must be: seam.*, package.*, node.*, promotion.*, corroboration.*, graph_patch.*, recovery.*, account.* — no surface-local shadow event language

Concern creation authority: runtime, package overseer, seam overseer, corroboration outcome, graph patch/state-transition logic may mint canonical concerns; workers may NOMINATE but not mint canonical concerns
gap_candidates.blocking_reason: Coverage row indicates incomplete or missing canon alignment for concrete target.
